citations.title: Review of label efficiency and robustness

claims.text: Method A achieves 0.92 accuracy on cohort X.
Method A requires large labeled data.
Method B is label-efficient but drops to 0.80 accuracy under domain shift.
A review notes no method combines label efficiency with robustness to domain shift.
The cited literature reveals a gap: label-efficient methods are not robust to domain shift.

paragraphs.text: Accurate prediction on cohort X is established: Method A achieves 0.92 accuracy [ref1]. However, Method A requires large labeled data [ref1], motivating label-efficient alternatives.
Approaches differ in label efficiency and robustness. Method A is accurate but label-hungry [ref1]; Method B is label-efficient yet drops to 0.80 accuracy under domain shift [ref2].
A recent review notes that no method combines label efficiency with robustness to domain shift [ref3].
Taken together, the cited literature reveals a gap: label-efficient methods are not robust to domain shift [ref1][ref2][ref3].
This work targets the label-efficiency/robustness gap identified above (proposed contribution; actual results not in the provided material).

research_gap.statement: Label-efficient methods lack robustness to domain shift.

contributions.text: Proposed: a label-efficient method robust to domain shift, addressing the gap.
